Yes—**a Fly Volume fits the auth implementation we just added.** It gives you a writable directory that survives deployments and restarts. Fly’s regular root filesystem is ephemeral. [Fly Volume docs](https://docs.fly.io/volumes/overview)

I’d use:

|---|---|
| Twitch client ID and client secret | Fly secrets |
| Rotating access and refresh tokens | `/data/twitch-tokens.json` on a volume |
| Existing SQLite database | Same `/data` volume |

Your checked-in [fly.toml](/home/marek/code/twitch/twitch-alerts/fly.toml) currently has no volume mount, although your startup script already uses `/data/db`.

If you don’t already have a volume, create one in your configured region:

```bash
fly volumes create alerts_data --region atl --size 1
```

Add this to `fly.toml`:

```toml
[[mounts]]
  source = "alerts_data"
  destination = "/data"
```

Then add this to the existing `[env]` section:

```toml
TWITCH_TOKEN_FILE = "/data/twitch-tokens.json"
```

Keep the application credentials in [Fly secrets](https://docs.fly.io/apps/secrets):

```bash
fly secrets set TWITCH_CLIENT_ID=... TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET=...
```

Run the one-time authorization against that persistent token file. Subsequent renewals save there automatically.
